h1: Private Jet to Tijuana from Mexico City
hero_sub: Baja Med kitchens, the vineyards of Valle de Guadalupe and the Pacific at Rosarito, three hours and ten minutes from Toluca.
answer: A private jet to Tijuana from Mexico City takes about 3 hours 10 minutes nonstop from Toluca (AIT) to Tijuana International (TIJ), and the full aircraft starts at $12,000 USD one way. Crew, fuel, catering and permits are included. Because it is a domestic flight, the aircraft can be ready about 2 hours after you confirm, and your quote arrives on WhatsApp within 30 minutes.
story: Tijuana has outgrown every label it was given. The old souvenir strip of Avenida Revolución now shares the street with craft breweries and cocktail bars, and chefs from Zona Río to Playas de Tijuana cook a style the rest of Mexico calls Baja Med: Pacific seafood, olive oil and northern Mexican fire. It is also home to the busiest land crossing in the Western Hemisphere, a city where doctors, factories and families work on both sides of the line every day.

Getting there from central Mexico is the hard part. Commercial schedules work for some trips, while a private jet to Tijuana lets you set the hour, bring the whole team and land at TIJ in about three hours. Patients arrive rested for their appointment. Executives visit a plant in Otay Mesa and fly home the same evening. Couples land in the morning and are pouring a glass of Baja Nebbiolo in Valle de Guadalupe by early afternoon.
why_title: Why fly a private jet to Tijuana

why.d: Tijuana is a domestic route, so there is no US customs paperwork and no international permit to wait for. Once you confirm, the aircraft can be ready in about 2 hours, which matters when a surgery date moves or a client meeting appears on short notice.

From $12,000 USD one way covers the full jet with crew, fuel, catering and permits. Split across a family or a work team, one fare covers everyone, and the group travels on the schedule you choose. Larger cabins are quoted on WhatsApp in 30 minutes.

Tijuana draws patients from across Mexico and the United States for dental, bariatric and cosmetic procedures. A private cabin means quiet, space to stretch out, no long walks through terminals and a seat for whoever is coming along. On the way home, that comfort matters even more.

From TIJ you are about 30 to 40 minutes from the beaches of Rosarito, roughly an hour and a half to two hours from Valle de Guadalupe, and a short drive from the San Ysidro crossing into San Diego. One landing opens the whole northern coast.

journey_title: Your day from Polanco to Tijuana

journey.d: Your driver collects you before the morning traffic builds. Toluca is 45 to 60 minutes west by road, or about 25 minutes by JETCAB helicopter from Polanco, Lomas, Santa Fe or Reforma if you would rather skip the highway.

Your car stops at the private terminal and you reach the aircraft steps in under 10 minutes. On a domestic flight your official ID is all you show. Bags go straight into the hold and breakfast is already loaded on board.

Wheels up. The route crosses western Mexico toward the Gulf of California and the Sonoran desert, with the ridges of the Sierra Madre Occidental below the wing on a clear day. Work, sleep or eat at your own pace.

You land at Tijuana International around 9:25 am Pacific time in winter, after about 3 hours 10 minutes. The airport sits right on the border in Otay Mesa. With no customs on a domestic arrival, your car is ready within minutes.

Zona Río, the business and dining district along the Tijuana River, is about 15 minutes away. Start with coffee and a Baja breakfast, then head to your appointment, your plant visit or the coast road south to Rosarito.

places_title: What to do in Tijuana after you land

places.name: Avenida Revolución
places.d: The city's most famous street still has its arch and murals, while the nightlife has moved upmarket. Caesar's, where the Caesar salad was created in the 1920s, still tosses it tableside. Then explore the passages off the avenue, where galleries and small bars have taken over old storefronts.

places.name: Centro Cultural Tijuana
places.d: Locals call it La Bola for its giant spherical dome, which houses a domed cinema. Opened in 1982, the complex holds the Museo de las Californias, an aquarium and rotating art exhibitions. It is the best single introduction to the city's history and its place between two countries.

places.name: Valle de Guadalupe
places.d: Mexico's best-known wine region lies inland from Ensenada, with more than a hundred wineries spread over rolling, sunburned hills. Lunch at an open-air kitchen, taste Nebbiolo and Tempranillo grown in Baja soil, and stay in a cabin among the vines. Harvest festivals fill the summer calendar.

places.name: Rosarito
places.d: A beach town about half an hour south of the city, Rosarito has wide sand, surf breaks and seafood stands along the old coast road. Puerto Nuevo, a few kilometers further south, is famous for lobster served with rice, beans and flour tortillas. Watch the sunset from a cliff-top terrace.

best_time_title: When to fly a private jet to Tijuana
best_time: Tijuana has a dry, mild climate shaped by the Pacific. Summer days sit in the high 70s and low 80s°F, winters are cool with most of the year's rain falling between December and March, and spring mornings often start under coastal fog. July and August are harvest season in Valle de Guadalupe, when the Fiestas de la Vendimia bring tastings and long dinners among the vines, so reserve lodging early. For medical or business trips, any month works. Domestic flights can be ready about 2 hours after you confirm, though a day's notice gives you the widest choice of aircraft.
airport: Tijuana International, officially General Abelardo L. Rodríguez International Airport, sits in Otay Mesa with its runway running alongside the US border fence. Private aircraft use the general aviation side, away from the commercial terminal. Because your flight from Toluca is domestic, there is no customs or immigration on arrival. Zona Río is about 15 minutes away, Playas de Tijuana about 25, Rosarito 30 to 40 and Valle de Guadalupe roughly an hour and a half to two hours. The Cross Border Xpress bridge to the San Diego side connects to the commercial terminal.
docs_title: Documents for a private flight to Tijuana
docs: Tijuana is a domestic flight, so Mexican citizens only need an official photo ID such as the INE or a passport. Foreign passengers carry their passport and the immigration record they entered Mexico with. Send the passenger names when you book so the manifest is ready. If you plan to cross into San Diego during the trip, bring your passport and a valid US visa, since the land border formalities still apply.

faq.q: How long is a private jet flight from Mexico City to Tijuana?
faq.a: About 3 hours 10 minutes nonstop from Toluca (AIT) to Tijuana International (TIJ), a distance of roughly 2,600 km. Tijuana runs on Pacific time, one to two hours behind Mexico City, so a jet leaving Toluca at 8:15 am lands at about 9:25 am local time in winter.

faq.q: How much does a private jet to Tijuana cost?
faq.a: A private jet to Tijuana from Mexico City starts at $12,000 USD one way for the full aircraft, with crew, fuel, catering and permits included. If you need a larger cabin or a same-day return, JETCAB confirms the exact price on WhatsApp within 30 minutes.

faq.q: Do I need a passport to fly private to Tijuana?
faq.a: Mexican citizens do not. Toluca to Tijuana is a domestic route, so an official photo ID such as the INE is enough. Foreign visitors carry their passport and Mexican entry record. Anyone planning to continue to San Diego by land needs a passport and a valid US visa.

faq.q: Can I reach San Diego from Tijuana after landing?
faq.a: Yes. The San Ysidro and Otay Mesa crossings are a short drive from TIJ, though car lines can be long at peak hours. If San Diego is your real destination, a direct private jet to San Diego takes about 3 hours 20 minutes from $9,000 USD and skips the land border entirely.

faq.q: How much is a private jet to Cabo?
faq.a: From Mexico City, a private jet to Los Cabos (SJD) takes about 2 hours 30 minutes and starts at $3,800 USD one way on a Learjet 35 for up to 7 passengers. You can also pair both ends of Baja in one trip, with business in Tijuana and a few days at the tip of the peninsula.

faq.q: Do you tip a private jet pilot?
faq.a: It is not required, and no tip is ever added to a JETCAB quote, since the price already covers the crew. If someone on board went out of their way for you or your family, a gratuity is a personal gesture left entirely to your judgment.
